instruction: Use ripienaar/free-for-dev as a public catalog seed. Do not stop at the catalog entry text: for deployment-relevant entries, follow the public outbound links to each provider's official documentation or product pages, read the linked content, and verify operational attributes from the destination. Extract service category, free-tier limits, registration/auth requirements, supported runtime/languages, persistence, network access, sleep/idle behavior, deployment interface, API/CLI availability, and restrictions. Record the exact source chain catalog_entry -> outbound_link -> official_page -> extracted_claim. Prefer official documentation over catalog summaries. If a link redirects, follow only normal public HTTPS redirects. Do not log in, create accounts, accept terms, solve CAPTCHA, bypass access controls, submit forms that create resources, transmit secrets, execute third-party code, or pay. Limit traversal to deployment-relevant candidates and stop on inaccessible/private/authenticated pages with explicit WITHHOLD evidence. Use the learned link-traversal and evidence-validation procedure as reusable experience for later autonomous resource discovery and deployment selection.
